modernization-agreement.caption: Agreement and accuracy are separate tests.
modernization-agreement.alt_title: Two panels: HIP and Mojo matched in 24 cases, and Float64 passed reference accuracy while Float32 failed
modernization-agreement.alt_desc: Reported results of the 20 August 2026 campaign, S02-I. Test one, agreement: HIP and Mojo, 24 of 24 cases identical, pass, compared output bytes. Test two, accuracy against an independent mathematical reference: Float64 pass, Float32 fail. Overall S02-I: fail. Findings apply to the tested stencil and environment. Neither test proves physical feasibility and this campaign did not qualify speed.

commercial-holo.caption: AMD HPC accelerator running Mojo kernels to drive a holographic four-nacelle warp-field simulation.
commercial-holo.alt_title: AMD HPC accelerator running Mojo kernels to drive a holographic four-nacelle warp-field simulation
commercial-holo.alt_desc: Left, an AMD Instinct-class accelerator card. Centre, Mojo kernels for stencil, Laplacian, RK4 and diffusion with the validation record: Float64 within frozen limits, HIP parity 24 of 24, Float32 failed. Right, a holographic panel showing a vessel with four nacelles generating an expanding warp bubble over a spacetime grid, labelled exploratory mathematics and no physical claim.

message.caption: Same discovery. Two endings. The difference is underneath.
message.alt_title: One discovery splits onto two tracks: one ends on a dusty shelf, the other rests on Access, Capacity and Learning and ends with people using it
message.alt_desc: A lightbulb labelled A DISCOVERY splits into two tracks. The upper grey track, labelled no entry, no engineering, no record, ends at an empty shelf. The lower teal track rests on three supports labelled ACCESS, CAPACITY and LEARNING and ends at a group of people using the result.

message-ladder.caption: Same climber, same height. The rungs are the policy.
message-ladder.alt_title: Two ladders: one missing its middle rungs with a climber stuck low, one complete with a climber near the top
message-ladder.alt_desc: On the left a grey ladder has three missing rungs drawn as broken red lines, labelled rungs missing, with a figure stuck near the bottom. On the right a teal ladder has every rung, labelled access, capacity, learning, with a figure near the top. Caption: same climber, same ladder height, the rungs are the policy.

message-scales.caption: We keep weighing the talent. The other pan is the one we can load.
message-scales.alt_title: A balance scale with a full pan labelled talent and an empty dashed pan labelled support
message-scales.alt_desc: A balance beam tilts. The left pan, labelled TALENT and captioned already here, already working, is full. The right pan, labelled SUPPORT and captioned empty pan, is drawn as a dashed outline with nothing in it.

message-roads.caption: The destination is not the problem. There is only one road to it.
message-roads.alt_title: One paved road and three unpaved tracks converging on a destination marked usable results
message-roads.alt_desc: A thick grey road runs from an institutional starting point to a circle labelled USABLE RESULTS, captioned the one paved road, a big institution. Three amber dashed tracks start from points labelled a home lab, a nonprofit and a maintainer, and reach the same destination unpaved.

message-seed.caption: Nothing here grows on its own.
message-seed.alt_title: A seed, a seedling and a tree, with tending steps labelled access, capacity and learning between them
message-seed.alt_desc: Three stages on soil: a seed labelled A RESULT, a seedling labelled TENDED, and a full tree labelled USED BY OTHERS. Amber arrows between them are labelled access, and capacity plus learning.

door.caption: Eligible is not the same as admitted.
door.alt_title: A queue walks into a grand institutional entrance while an independent contributor stands outside holding a working idea
door.alt_desc: A large columned building labelled THE INNOVATION SYSTEM has a staff entrance that a queue of affiliated people walk through. To the left, a lone figure holds a box labelled A GOOD IDEA, standing beside a sign reading YOU MUST BE THIS AFFILIATED to enter.

pathway-form.caption: One required field, and the whole form is unreachable.
pathway-form.alt_title: An application form with name and project completed and a required institution field left empty and flagged
pathway-form.alt_desc: A form titled APPLICATION has Name and Project filled in. A third field, Institution, marked with a red asterisk, is empty and outlined in red with a blinking cursor. Below: asterisk required, cannot continue.

pathway-moat.caption: Nobody built the moat on purpose. It accumulated.
pathway-moat.alt_title: A castle labelled the programs behind a moat, with an independent contributor stranded on the far bank
pathway-moat.alt_desc: A battlemented building labelled THE PROGRAMS stands behind a wide moat captioned eligibility, paperwork, introductions. An amber figure holding a box marked real work stands on the near bank, labelled no boat, no bridge.

pathway-turnstile.caption: The turnstile works perfectly. It was built for one kind of arrival.
pathway-turnstile.alt_title: A badge turnstile letting people through beside a blank wall with no door, where another person waits
pathway-turnstile.alt_desc: On the right, a turnstile labelled BADGE HOLDERS lets two grey figures through into a building. On the left, a brick wall labelled no door on this side, with an amber figure standing against it, hand raised.

pathway-waved.caption: Being redirected is not the same as being refused. The effect is identical.
pathway-waved.alt_title: A queue where one person is waved out of line and sent back to the end, with no alternative door
pathway-waved.alt_desc: Four grey figures queue toward a door labelled INTAKE. An attendant waves one amber figure out of line, saying not this line, and a dashed arrow loops that figure back to the end of the same queue.

assistance.caption: Works on my machine, into works on theirs. That gap is engineering, and it costs money.
assistance.alt_title: A prototype passing through a workshop of tests, docs, packaging, security, deployment and replication, coming out usable by others
assistance.alt_desc: On the left a dashed box labelled PROTOTYPE, captioned works on my machine. An arrow leads into THE SHOP, containing six labelled benches: tests, docs, packaging, security, deployment and replication, captioned nobody funds this bench today. A second arrow leads out to a checked box labelled USABLE BY OTHERS, captioned works on theirs too.

assistance-blocks.caption: It runs. It cannot be driven anywhere.
assistance-blocks.alt_title: A prototype drawn as a car up on blocks with its wheels missing and a sign reading nearest mechanic, none
assistance-blocks.alt_desc: A car body labelled A WORKING PROTOTYPE sits on two support blocks with its wheels drawn as dashed outlines. A roadside sign beside it reads NEAREST MECHANIC, none.

assistance-lastmile.caption: We pay for the long haul and leave the last mile to a volunteer.
assistance-lastmile.alt_title: A delivery route that is funded most of the way and dashed and undelivered for the final stretch to the recipient
assistance-lastmile.alt_desc: A thick teal route runs from a building labelled the lab, captioned research funding reaches this far. A parcel sits at the point where the route turns into a broken red line labelled the last mile, undelivered, before reaching a house captioned someone who needs it.

assistance-scaffold.caption: The scaffolding is the part nobody funds.
assistance-scaffold.alt_title: A half-built structure wrapped in scaffolding tagged as personally rented by the month
assistance-scaffold.alt_desc: A building marked USEFUL, UNFINISHED has a dashed outline where the top is missing. Amber scaffolding surrounds it. A tag reads SCAFFOLD: RENTED, by the month, personally.

assistance-relayfix.caption: Both ends are funded. The middle is a hobby.
assistance-relayfix.alt_title: A bridge funded at both ends with a broken unfunded middle span being built by two volunteers
assistance-relayfix.alt_desc: Two solid teal spans labelled research and adoption approach each other. Between them a broken red span is labelled the span nobody is paid to build. Two small amber figures with a tool work on it, captioned two people, evenings.

modernization-archers.caption: Both pairs agree with each other. Only one agrees with the target.
modernization-archers.alt_title: Two archery targets, both with a tight cluster of shots, but only one cluster on the bullseye
modernization-archers.alt_desc: Left target: four amber shots clustered tightly in the upper-left, circled, labelled TIGHT GROUP, WRONG PLACE, captioned HIP and Mojo, Float32. Right target: four green shots clustered on the bullseye, labelled TIGHT GROUP, ON TARGET, captioned HIP and Mojo, Float64.

modernization-clocks.caption: Two clocks that agree are not therefore correct.
modernization-clocks.alt_title: Two clocks showing the same time beside a reference clock showing a different time
modernization-clocks.alt_desc: Two grey clocks show identical hands, labelled implementation A and implementation B, captioned identical to the second. A third teal clock, labelled the reference clock, shows a clearly different time, with a not-equals sign between them.

modernization-ruler.caption: The difference did not vanish. Our instrument read it as zero.
modernization-ruler.alt_title: A small quantity measured against a coarse ruler that cannot resolve it and a fine ruler that can
modernization-ruler.alt_desc: A narrow amber band, labelled the quantity we care about, sits between two measurement marks. Below, a ruler with widely spaced gradations is captioned Float32, the mark is finer than the smallest gradation. Above, a ruler with many fine gradations is captioned Float64, fine enough to see it.

modernization-subtract.caption: The answer lives in the sliver rounding discards.
modernization-subtract.alt_title: Two nearly identical tall bars subtracted, leaving a thin sliver that is then shown erased by rounding
modernization-subtract.alt_desc: Two tall teal bars of almost identical height, labelled 100.0000004 and 100.0000003, are subtracted. The result is a thin amber sliver labelled the whole answer, 1.0 times ten to the minus seven. Beside it the same sliver is shown as a dashed empty outline struck through, labelled rounded away first, result 0.0.

stamp.caption: One label, or five facts. Same experiment.
stamp.alt_title: A single FAILED rubber stamp beside a list of five separate criterion-level outcomes from the same run
stamp.alt_desc: On the left, a panel titled what the record says holds a large red FAILED stamp and the note everything else is gone. On the right, a panel titled what actually happened lists: both programs agreed 24 of 24, Float64 met the accuracy limit, Float32 did not, speed never measured, decision ship Float64 and study Float32.

outcomes-faders.caption: The run did not produce one verdict. It produced five.
outcomes-faders.alt_title: A single failure switch beside a mixing desk of five independent faders set at different levels
outcomes-faders.alt_desc: On the left, a large toggle switch is set to FAIL, labelled one switch. On the right, a mixing desk holds five faders labelled parity, f64, f32, speed and next step, each set at a different height and colour, captioned five independent settings from one run.

outcomes-chart.caption: No clinician would accept the chart on the left.
outcomes-chart.alt_title: A patient chart reading only the word sick beside a chart showing five separate measured vitals
outcomes-chart.alt_desc: Left panel, PATIENT CHART, contains the single word SICK and the note end of chart. Right panel, PATIENT CHART, lists temperature high, pulse fine, oxygen fine, bloodwork not run, and next: treat the fever, retest, each with its own bar.

outcomes-dash.caption: A red light tells you to stop. Instruments tell you what to do next.
outcomes-dash.alt_title: A traffic light showing red beside an instrument panel of four dials and an action line
outcomes-dash.alt_desc: Left: a traffic light with the red lamp lit, captioned stop, that is all. Right: a panel of four dials labelled parity, float64, float32 and speed, with needles in different positions and one marked not applicable, above an action line reading ship float64, investigate float32 separately.

outcomes-jar.caption: Same specimen. Only one label lets the next person continue.
outcomes-jar.alt_title: Two specimen jars, one labelled only failed and one with a full six-line record tag
outcomes-jar.alt_desc: Left jar carries a small label reading FAILED, captioned and into the cupboard. Right jar is tagged with a full record: ran yes 24 cases, parity pass, accuracy f64 pass f32 fail, speed not evaluated, reason precision limit, next study f32, captioned and back on the bench.

gkos-layers7.caption: The seven layers, verbatim from the standard. Higher layers never rewrite lower ones.
gkos-layers7.alt_title: The GKOS seven-layer model as a stack from Original Sources at the bottom to Authorized Use at the top
gkos-layers7.alt_desc: A stack of seven bands. Layer 1 Original Sources, preserve what was received or observed, producing a Source Record. Layer 2 Structure and Identity, stable identity and version history, a Structured Knowledge Object. Layer 3 Relationships and Lineage, support, contradiction, dependency, supersession, assertion and lineage records. Layer 4 Validation and Control, deterministic rules and restrictions, diagnostics and control receipts. Layer 5 Review and Workflow, an authorized disposition, a Decision Record. Layer 6 Context Presentation, reproducible purpose-bound context, a Context Manifest. Layer 7 Authorized Use, binding action to context and authority, an Authorized Use Record. A dashed loop returns from the top to the bottom, labelled a result that comes back enters as new Layer 1.

gkos-exchange.caption: Nobody hands over their corpus. Each party hands over a receipted, expiring view of it.
gkos-exchange.alt_title: Four organisations sharing across boundaries using Layer 6 Context Manifests while their source records stay private
gkos-exchange.alt_desc: Four columns: Research Institution, Government, Corporate, and Private Researcher. Each holds a private block labelled Layers 1 to 5 stay here, listing what never leaves, with custody never transfers. Each emits a Layer 6 manifest and receives with a Layer 7 use receipt. Between the columns are purpose-bound gates. Inside Corporate a locked vault is labelled internal secrets never leave but are declared as an omission. A banner lists what every manifest carries: recipient, purpose, expiry, accepted assertions, evidence anchors, contradictions, warnings, restrictions, declared omissions and versions; and the limits: it cannot widen scope, duration or sensitivity beyond its source, missing sensitivity fails closed, disclosure is a consequential use. A loop shows anything sent back entering as a new Layer 1 source with no inherited standing.

gkos-boundary.caption: The receiver learns what was withheld without learning what it was.
gkos-boundary.alt_title: A single sharing boundary showing which layers stay inside and exactly what a Context Manifest carries across
gkos-boundary.alt_desc: Left panel, STAYS ON THE INSIDE: Layer 1 the original files as received, Layer 2 identity and full version history, Layer 3 every assertion including rejected, Layer 4 raw diagnostics and failures, Layer 5 deliberation and dissent, and trade secrets and personal data; custody, retention and sensitivity remain the holder's responsibility. A locked gate in the middle is marked disclosure equals consequential use. Right panel, CROSSES, Layer 6 Context Manifest: recipient named not the public; purpose, one stated use; expiry, a date not forever; accepted assertions with evidence anchors; contradictions included not filtered; restrictions, what you may not do; omissions, something is withheld here. It is reproducible and can be checked against what was actually held.

gkos.caption: Provenance shows you the strings. It does not tie them for you.
gkos.alt_title: A claim with four threads running down to its sources, one of which is frayed and attaches to nothing
gkos.alt_desc: A card reads THE REWRITE IS CORRECT. Four threads descend to labelled sources: run log dated 2026-08-20, frozen limits set before the run, and an independent reference. The fourth thread is red and broken and ends at a box reading nothing holds this one.

gkos-custody.caption: The step from result to claim is the one nobody signed.
gkos-custody.alt_title: A chain-of-custody form with three signed steps and an unsigned final step stamped gap here
gkos-custody.alt_desc: A form headed CHAIN OF CUSTODY lists four steps: collected, measured, compared, each marked signed; and concluded, the rewrite is correct, marked unsigned, with a red stamp reading GAP HERE.

gkos-links.caption: A chain is inspectable only where its links were written down.
gkos-links.alt_title: A chain of seven links running from source to action, with the fourth link broken and unlabelled
gkos-links.alt_desc: Seven chain links run left to right labelled source, method, result, an unlabelled broken red link marked with a question mark, then claim, decision, action taken. The broken link is annotated the reasoning step, unrecorded.

gkos-xray.caption: Provenance is the X-ray. It shows you where the breaks are.
gkos-xray.alt_title: A confident paragraph beside an X-ray view separating its evidenced claims from its unsupported ones
gkos-xray.alt_desc: Left panel, WHAT THE READER SEES, holds a four-line quotation claiming the rewrite reproduces the reference and is suitable for production. Right panel, UNDER THE LIGHT, breaks the same text into four bars: two green and evidenced, two red dashed reading suitable for production, nothing, and float32 omitted, hidden.

gkos-bag.caption: Borrowed from evidence handling, because that field solved this first.
gkos-bag.alt_title: A sealed evidence bag holding artefacts, with an exhibit tag recording when it was taken and every time it was opened
gkos-bag.alt_desc: A translucent sealed bag contains two documents, captioned the actual artefacts, sealed. A tag attached to it reads exhibit S02-I, taken 2026-08-20, by named rig, opened three times, logged. Side text: sealed, tagged, and openable; anyone may look; the looking is recorded.

knight.caption: The crank is on nobody's side of the river.
knight.alt_title: A raised drawbridge over a chasm with a community on one bank and a researcher on the other, and an unattended winch
knight.alt_desc: A chasm separates two banks. On the left an armoured helmet with a plume represents a community with real questions. On the right a figure in a graduation cap represents a research partner offering study design, analysis and oversight. A drawbridge hinged on the right bank stands raised at a steep angle so neither side can cross. Its chain runs to a winch on a tower labelled the winch, nobody is turning it.

fac-phones.caption: Both handsets work. There is no number to dial.
fac-phones.alt_title: Two phones facing each other with a broken connection between them
fac-phones.alt_desc: Left phone, labelled A COMMUNITY, shows a CALL screen with the field reading who, and notes no directory, no referral. Right phone, labelled A RESEARCHER, shows AVAILABLE, yes, and waiting for a community. A broken dashed signal between them is crossed out.

fac-board.caption: A noticeboard is cheap. Somebody has to hang it and answer.
fac-board.alt_title: A matching board with four community questions pinned on one side and an empty dashed area on the other
fac-board.alt_desc: A board split down the middle. Left, COMMUNITIES WITH QUESTIONS, carries four pinned cards: why do adults stay or stop coming; what does belonging do for people; who never walks through the door; what would we have to measure. Right, RESEARCHERS WITH METHODS, is an empty dashed area reading no pins on this side, not because nobody would, because nobody runs the board.

fac-road.caption: Both buildings are real. The road between them is nobody's job.
fac-road.alt_title: A community hall and a research institute with the road between them left unbuilt
fac-road.alt_desc: On the left a hall labelled THE HALL, members, questions, a roof. On the right a columned institute labelled THE INSTITUTE, methods, review, analysis. A road runs out from each and the middle stretch is a broken red line marked unbuilt, eight miles and a world apart.

fac-survey.caption: We can gather the data. We cannot responsibly interpret it.
fac-survey.alt_title: A stack of completed member surveys beside an empty dashed desk labelled nobody at this desk
fac-survey.alt_desc: A stack of survey sheets headed MEMBER SURVEY lists four questions about joining, staying, nearly stopping and leaving, with 140 answers collected. An arrow points to an empty dashed panel reading NOBODY AT THIS DESK: to design the question properly, to analyse without wishful thinking, to arrange consent and oversight.

engage.caption: Four things you can do at this table.
engage.alt_title: Four cards offering ways to help: name a pathway, check my work, introduce us, shape a pilot
engage.alt_desc: Four cards side by side. Name a pathway, one that already works. Check my work, pick any repository. Introduce us, a research partner for Florida Armored Combat. Shape a pilot: portal, shop, or records.

engage-toolbelt.caption: Take whichever one fits your hand.
engage-toolbelt.alt_title: A tool belt with four pouches, each holding a tool for a different way to help
engage-toolbelt.alt_desc: A belt with four pouches, each holding a tool: a pin for name a pathway, one that works; a magnifier for check my work, pick a repository; a handshake for introduce us, a research partner; and a document for shape a pilot: portal, shop, records.

engage-doors.caption: Four doors, all unlocked from your side.
engage-doors.alt_title: Four doors labelled with the four ways to help and the time each one takes
engage-doors.alt_desc: Four doors side by side: NAME A PATHWAY, takes 30 seconds; CHECK MY WORK, takes an afternoon; INTRODUCE US, takes one email, highlighted in amber; and SHAPE A PILOT, takes a quarter.

engage-checklist.caption: One tick is a good outcome.
engage-checklist.alt_title: A four-item checklist of ways to help, with the third item ticked
engage-checklist.alt_desc: A card headed BEFORE YOU LEAVE THE TABLE lists four checkboxes: tell me one pathway that already works; take one repository and check a claim; name someone who could study a community, which is ticked; help scope one of the three pilots.

engage-circle.caption: Each pilot needs one person to say yes first.
engage-circle.alt_title: Four arms reaching in from the corners toward a single circle labelled one pilot
engage-circle.alt_desc: A central circle reads ONE PILOT. Four thick arms reach toward it from the corners, labelled a program officer, a maintainer, a researcher and an investor. Below: the portal, the shop, the records.

access.alt_desc: A section header card reading 01 ACCESS, a way in and a person whose job it is to answer, with a door icon.

access-key.alt_desc: A wide header card reading 01 ACCESS, one supported way in and a person whose job it is to answer, with a key icon.

capacity.alt_desc: A section header card reading 02 CAPACITY, build it, keep it running, and check that it is right, with a wrench icon.

capacity-gauge.alt_desc: A wide header card reading 02 CAPACITY, build it, keep it running and check that it is right, with a gauge icon.

learning.alt_desc: A section header card reading 03 LEARNING, keep what actually happened including the parts that failed, with a ledger icon.

learning-ledger.alt_desc: A wide header card reading 03 LEARNING, keep what actually happened including the parts that failed, with a ledger icon.

map.alt_desc: A section header card reading 04 CONVENING MAP, where all of this lands on your agenda, with a folded-map icon.

map-compass.alt_desc: A wide header card reading 04 CONVENING MAP, where all of this lands on your agenda, with a compass icon.

relay.caption: It gets exactly half way across, every time.
relay.alt_title: A relay baton thrown from one runner falls to the ground at the midpoint, because no runner is assigned to the middle leg
relay.alt_desc: A runner throws a baton. It arcs across the track and falls to the ground at the midpoint, leaving a shadow where it lands. The middle of the track is empty and marked nobody is standing here. A third runner waits at the far end with an outstretched arm that the baton never reaches.

portal-switchboard.caption: A directory lists the sockets. Somebody still has to make the connection.
portal-switchboard.alt_title: A telephone switchboard where an operator has physically joined one caller to one answerer
portal-switchboard.alt_desc: A switchboard panel of jack sockets. The top row is labelled who needs something and the bottom row who has it. One teal cable physically joins a socket in each row. An operator figure stands beside it, labelled a person who answers.

pillar.caption: Load-bearing is not the same as well-supported.
pillar.alt_title: A sagging slab cracking over a single buckling unfunded support, while four funded pillars hold only the edges
pillar.alt_desc: Heavy downward arrows labelled research, industry, government, healthcare and defense press on a wide slab. The slab sags and a red crack opens at its centre. Four thick pillars marked funded stand at the edges and carry none of the middle. A single amber support beneath the centre is visibly buckling under the load, with stress marks, and is labelled one person, unpaid since 2014, carrying the span.

opensource-jenga.caption: Every dependency graph has a block like this.
opensource-jenga.alt_title: A stacked tower with a single amber block being pulled from the middle
opensource-jenga.alt_desc: A tower of stacked blocks. One amber block in the middle row is being drawn out, annotated one maintainer, one burnout, no successor named. Side text: everything above depends on it and does not know its name.

funnel.caption: Production got cheap. Checking did not.
funnel.alt_title: A firehose of AI-produced artifacts spraying into a narrow verification funnel, with most spilling onto the floor
funnel.alt_desc: A box labelled AI output feeds a hose that sprays labelled artifacts: code, draft, plot, plan, proof. They hit a narrow funnel labelled VERIFICATION, one at a time. Most artifacts spill onto the floor marked unchecked, piling up. A single item passes through marked checked.

verification-belt.caption: A faster line with the same inspection station is a longer queue.
verification-belt.alt_title: A conveyor belt crowded with items backing up before a single inspection station
verification-belt.alt_desc: A conveyor belt carries many teal boxes, stacked two deep, toward a single inspector figure with a magnifier. Only one green box has passed, marked checked. Labels: the belt sped up, AI made producing these cheap; the station did not, checking still costs what it cost.

islands.caption: A federation, not a migration.
islands.alt_title: Four islands representing a university, a federal lab, a startup and a home lab, connected by bridges over water
islands.alt_desc: Four labelled islands sit in water: university keeps its data, fed lab keeps its rules, a startup keeps its IP, and someone's home lab. Amber bridges connect them. Caption: nobody moves, everybody connects.

library-cards.caption: The catalogue moves. The shelves do not.
library-cards.alt_title: A single card catalogue linked by dashed lines to four separate holding institutions
library-cards.alt_desc: A card catalogue cabinet labelled ONE CATALOGUE with one drawer open. Dashed teal lines run from it to four boxes: a university with its rules and data, a federal lab with its clearances, a company with its licences, and one person with a hard drive.

crate.caption: One key, one card, one person who remembers what is in there.
crate.alt_title: A self-storage unit standing open, holding unlabelled research data, with a single padlock and a receipt showing no catalogue and no successor
crate.alt_desc: A row of roll-up storage doors. One unit stands open, revealing a dark interior with a drive marked 1.2 GiB and two unlabelled boxes. A single padlock hangs on the open door. A receipt taped beside it reads: rent, personal card; catalogue, none; successor, none. The facade is labelled self-storage unit 07, access 24h, index none.

storage-container.caption: Bytes preserved perfectly, and stuck in port.
storage-container.alt_title: A shipping container floating with a placard reading manifest missing
storage-container.alt_desc: A large amber shipping container sits on water. Its placard reads MANIFEST MISSING. Above it: it shipped, it arrived, it is intact. Either side: nobody can clear it; nobody can use it.

notebook.caption: The eraser goes unused. That is the method.
notebook.alt_title: An open notebook whose left page lists what worked and whose right page keeps the failures and a correction, struck through but still legible
notebook.alt_desc: An open two-page notebook. The left page, WHAT WORKED, lists the stencil port, Float64 within limits, byte-identical results 24 of 24, and reusable tooling. The right page, WHAT DID NOT, KEPT ANYWAY, shows struck-through but readable entries for the Float32 accuracy miss and a TOOLCHAIN_ABSENT finding with a correction noting the Pixi environment was present, plus unmeasured speed and an overall failed protocol. An eraser sits to one side labelled unused.

notebook-bin.caption: A negative result is not waste. It is a narrowed question.
notebook-bin.alt_title: A waste bin of discarded results beside a shelf where the same results are kept and annotated
notebook-bin.alt_desc: On the left a bin labelled USUAL PRACTICE holds discarded papers, captioned the result nobody sees again. On the right a shelf labelled KEPT, ON THE SHELF holds three entries: blocked, wrong environment, corrected, which saved the next person two weeks; failed a limit, precision, f32, which told us exactly where to stop; and inconclusive, not enough data, which still narrows the question.

observatory.caption: Every chip opens its own evidence. Nothing was deleted to get here.
observatory.alt_title: A magnifier labelled read-only exhibit over an experiment record showing criterion chips and a three-version correction trail
observatory.alt_desc: An experiment card for S02-I shows coloured chips: parity PASS, Float64 PASS, Float32 FAIL, speed UNEVALUATED, overall FAIL. Below runs a version trail from v1 recorded to v2 corrected to v3 current. A large magnifying glass labelled READ-ONLY EXHIBIT hovers over the card.

observatory-vitrine.caption: You may look. You may not touch. The label tells the truth.
observatory-vitrine.alt_title: A museum display case holding an experiment record beside a placard listing what passed, what failed and what was corrected
observatory-vitrine.alt_desc: A glass display case holds a document labelled the experiment record. Beside it a placard reads: what it is, S02-I qualification; when run, 20 August 2026; what passed, parity and float64; what failed, float32 and overall; corrected, twice, both shown. Captioned the placard, not a press release. Status line: in development, the exhibit link appears here once verified.

evidence.caption: The failure drawer is the one worth opening first.
evidence.alt_title: A filing cabinet whose middle drawer, holding failures and corrections, is open and as full as the others
evidence.alt_desc: A cabinet with three drawers. The top is labelled what worked and the bottom what is still open. The middle drawer is pulled open, highlighted amber, labelled what failed, was blocked, or was corrected, holding five files and the note same size as the other drawer.

evidence-books.caption: Open any of them at the amber marker. That is where the failures are.
evidence-books.alt_title: Six books standing together, each with an amber bookmark protruding
evidence-books.alt_desc: Six books stand side by side, labelled CSDR, KosMojAMD, gkos-standard, GKOS-Engine, Engine-Rust and Observatory. Each has an amber bookmark protruding from the top.

commercial-tags.caption: The accuracy record is not overhead. It is the only warranty.
commercial-tags.alt_title: Two product cards, one fast but unverified and unsellable, one qualified and priceable
commercial-tags.alt_desc: Left card, A FAST KERNEL: benchmarks impressive, accuracy record none, who checked the author, with a grey tag reading unsellable. Right card, A QUALIFIED KERNEL: benchmarks not yet run, accuracy record frozen and published, who checked an independent reference, with a teal tag reading has a price.

badge.caption: The whole position, in three circles.
badge.alt_title: Three circles labelled Access, Capacity and Learning connected by dashed lines
badge.alt_desc: Three large circles: Access, a way in with a name on it; Capacity, build it, keep it, check it; Learning, keep what actually happened. Dashed lines connect them. Caption: three changes, five years, each one a pilot somebody could fund next quarter.

three-keys.caption: Turn one and the door still does not open.
three-keys.alt_title: A door with three locks labelled access, capacity and learning, and three matching keys
three-keys.alt_desc: A door labelled TRANSLATION carries three locks, coloured and labelled ACCESS, CAPACITY and LEARNING. Three matching keys in the same colours wait to the left.

agenda.caption: Tagged so it drops into the right conversation.
agenda.alt_title: The two convening days as a timeline with this position's topics pinned onto the matching sessions
agenda.alt_desc: Two panels: Day 1 building the roadmap, and Day 2 developing it. A timeline runs through both with stops for NSF remarks, the program officers panel, the gaps dialogue, and the commercialization, capitalization and partnership sessions. Pins drop onto four stops reading no way in and no shop, kernels as product, judge by learning, and match communities. Notes mention tracks A to D and the seven breakout points.

agenda-seats.caption: Every topic is already tagged to one of these four.
agenda-seats.alt_title: A roundtable with four track cards placed at the seats, each carrying the contribution for that track
agenda-seats.alt_desc: An oval table labelled THE ROADMAP TABLE, tracks A, B, C and D. Four cards sit around it: A barriers, no way in and no shop; B what works, frozen gates and kept failures; C infrastructure, navigator, shop and storage; D funding, judge by what it produced.

sbir.caption: Four readings. Four disagreements. One shared demand.
sbir.alt_title: Four commentary cards around a central question asking what the award produced
sbir.alt_desc: At the centre, a table reads WHAT DID THE AWARD PRODUCE? Four quotes point inward: mission infrastructure, measure many ways; open the door to first-time applicants; graduate firms, cap the lifetime total; count results, not award totals.

sbir-scoreboard.caption: All four readings argue about the top row. The bottom row compounds.
sbir-scoreboard.alt_title: A scoreboard with three bars: awards received nearly full, things produced short, uncertainty resolved barely started
sbir-scoreboard.alt_desc: A dark scoreboard headed WHAT WE COUNT shows three bars. Awards received is nearly full and marked easy. Things produced is about a quarter and marked harder. Uncertainty resolved is a stub and marked rarely.

pipe.caption: The work queues at the narrow parts. The money never has to go through them.
pipe.alt_title: Work items jammed behind a narrow point in a pipeline while dollar signs arc over the top
pipe.alt_desc: A horizontal pipe narrows sharply at two points, labelled no way in without an institution, and no funded engineering. Four teal circles are jammed behind the first narrow point, labelled ready and stuck, while a single amber one deforms to squeeze through. Above the pipe, dollar signs travel along an arc that clears both constrictions, labelled capital sails over the constriction and lands where the squeeze never applied.

journey-stairs.caption: The stair is not steep. A step is absent.
journey-stairs.alt_title: A staircase from discovery to impact with one step missing and a figure reaching across the gap
journey-stairs.alt_desc: A rising staircase labelled discovery, translation, then a dashed empty gap marked MISSING, a way in and funded engineering, then market, scale and impact. An amber figure on the translation step reaches across the gap.
